verdict.summary:
PRC-024-3 COMPLIANCE DETERMINATION — R4 RESPONSE CLOCK, CHANGE-REPORTING EXCEPTION, AND R1–R4 EVIDENCE RETENTION

=====================================================================
0. VERSION CONTROL AND SCOPING (satisfies ask 1, the constraint)
=====================================================================

Controlling text: "PRC-024-3 — Frequency and Voltage Protection Settings for Generating Resources," as posted by NERC at https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/standards/reliability-standards/prc/prc-024-3.pdf, retrieved 2026-11-23T20:02:48Z (sha256 941a2187c37f). The retrieval date is two days after the as-of date of 2026-11-21, so the posted document is the version in force on 2026-11-21 unless a revision became effective inside that 48-hour window. If a successor standard (e.g., an IBR ride-through standard arising from FERC's IBR rulemaking) had taken effect for the applicable Generator Owner by 2026-11-21, the requirement numbering and the clocks below would have to be re-derived; nothing in the retrieved record indicates that.

Documents deliberately NOT relied on, and why: the 2019-04-17 redline (PRC-024-3_Redline_04172019.pdf) and the Alberta and New Brunswick filing exhibits. These carry proposed or redline language — "generator protection trip settings," and applicability to "Generator Owner or Transmission Owner" — that does not match the approved requirement text. Using them would overstate who the obligation binds and would misquote the object of the submittal. Cite the posted standard only.

Who owes what: R4 binds the Generator Owner. The counterparty is the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the associated generating resource(s). Where more than one entity models the resource, respond to the entity that issued the written request; M4 requires you to hold a copy of that request.

Unit convention: NERC expresses these clocks in calendar days, not business days. The quoted text says "calendar days" explicitly.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWERS (one line each, matching the results array)
=====================================================================

Ask 2 — Time to provide R1/R2 protection settings after a written request from the PC/TP that models the resource:
    60 CALENDAR DAYS from receipt of the written request. (PRC-024-3, Requirement R4)

Ask 3 — Deadline after a change to previously requested settings, and the exception:
    60 CALENDAR DAYS from the change, unless the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner directs that reporting of protection setting changes is not required. (PRC-024-3, Requirement R4)

Ask 4 — Retention of data/evidence for Requirements R1 through R4:
    3 CALENDAR YEARS. (PRC-024-3, Compliance section — Evidence Retention; covers Requirements R1–R4 and Measures M1–M4.)

Ask 1 — constraint, no numeric result: the operative standard is PRC-024-3 as posted (retrieved 2026-11-23), which is the version in force on 2026-11-21.

=====================================================================
2. VERBATIM REQUIREMENT TEXT (quoted, not paraphrased)
=====================================================================

Requirement R4:
"R4. Each Generator Owner shall provide its applicable protection settings associated with Requirements R1 and R2 to the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the associated generating resource(s) within 60 calendar days of receipt of a written request for the data and within 60 calendar days of any change to those previously requested settings unless directed by the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that the reporting of protection setting changes is not required. [Violation Risk Factor: Lower] [Time Horizon: Operations Planning]"

Measure M4:
"M4. Each Generator Owner shall have evidence that it communicated applicable protection settings in accordance with Requirement R4, such as dated e-mails, correspondence or other evidence and copies of any requests it has received for that information."

Three operative elements, and only three: (a) a 60-calendar-day clock triggered by receipt of a written request; (b) a 60-calendar-day clock triggered by a change to the settings previously requested; (c) a conditional exception that can only be granted by the requesting PC/TP and that reaches only element (b).

=====================================================================
3. HOW TO COUNT THE CLOCK (procedure)
=====================================================================

Step 1 — Identify the trigger date. For element (a): the date the written request is received (not the date it was sent, and not the date someone in the organization first reads it). For element (b): the date the setting change is made/becomes effective.

Step 2 — Day of the trigger = day 0. Day 1 is the next calendar day. The deadline is the end of day 60. Calendar days include Saturdays, Sundays and holidays; the standard provides no business-day convention and no weekend/holiday roll-forward.

Worked example, written request:
    Request received 2026-11-21  -> day 0
    Day 1 = 2026-11-22 ... day 9 = 2026-11-30 (9 days left in November)
    Day 10 = 2026-12-01 ... day 40 = 2026-12-31 (31 days in December)
    Day 41 = 2027-01-01 ... day 60 = 2027-01-20
    DEADLINE: 2027-01-20.

Worked example, change to previously requested settings:
    Change effective 2026-12-01 -> day 0
    Day 1 = 2026-12-02 ... day 30 = 2026-12-31
    Day 31 = 2027-01-01 ... day 60 = 2027-01-30
    DEADLINE: 2027-01-30.

Step 3 — Target internal completion at day 45–50, not day 60. Day 60 is the outer legal limit; there is no grace period and no cure window (see section 7).

Step 4 — Date-stamp the transmittal. The evidence required by M4 is proof of communication, so the submittal must be dated and retained (dated e-mail, correspondence, or equivalent). An undated or unattributable submittal does not demonstrate compliance even if it was in fact sent on time.

=====================================================================
4. THE CHANGE-REPORTING EXCEPTION — CONDITIONS AND LIMITS
=====================================================================

The exception reads: "...unless directed by the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that the reporting of protection setting changes is not required." Read it narrowly:

(a) Who can grant it: only the requesting PC/TP — the entity that issued the original written request (or that models the resource and made the request). A direction from a different Planning Coordinator, a different Transmission Planner, or an internal manager does not trigger the exception.

(b) Form: it must be a direction. Obtain it in writing (dated e-mail is sufficient) and retain it under M4 alongside the request and the submittal. An undocumented verbal understanding is unprovable at audit and will be treated as no direction at all.

(c) Scope: it relieves only the obligation to report changes to previously requested settings. It does NOT:
    - relieve or extend the 60-calendar-day response to the original written request;
    - relieve the underlying R1/R2 obligation to set protective relaying within the applicable no-trip zone (or within a Transmission Planner's less-stringent allowed settings);
    - touch R3's separate obligation to document and communicate known regulatory or equipment limitations, which runs on its own shorter clock (the R3 Violation Severity Level grid in the posted standard begins escalating above 30 calendar days);
    - relieve the obligation to respond to a fresh written request for the data.

(d) Silence is not a direction. If no direction exists, the 60-day change clock runs for every change, without exception.

(e) Withdrawal: if the PC/TP later rescinds the direction, the 60-day clock applies to changes occurring after the rescission date. Record the rescission date and retain it; do not apply the rescission retroactively to changes already made while the direction was in force.

(f) Good practice: maintain a one-line register per generating resource — resource ID, PC/TP of record, date of last written request, date of last submittal, whether a change-reporting direction is on file and its date, and a change log of setting changes with the resulting 60-day due date.

=====================================================================
5. WHAT COUNTS AS "A CHANGE TO THOSE PREVIOUSLY REQUESTED SETTINGS"
=====================================================================

The clock attaches to a change in the settings previously provided in response to the request — i.e., the applicable protection settings associated with R1 and R2 for that resource. Practical triggers to log:
    - revised protective relay setpoints or trip settings within the R1/R2 scope (frequency, voltage, volts-per-hertz elements) arising from a periodic settings review;
    - settings changed as a result of relay or equipment replacement or firmware/settings migration;
    - settings revised at the direction of the Transmission Planner (including a location-specific study that permits less-stringent voltage settings under R2);
    - correction of an error in a previously submitted package.
Establish a documented change-detection step (compare as-built relay settings against the last submitted package) so the 60-day clock is started on the actual change date rather than discovered at the next audit.

=====================================================================
6. EVIDENCE RETENTION FOR R1 THROUGH R4 (ask 4)
=====================================================================

Period: THREE CALENDAR YEARS. PRC-024-3's Compliance section (Evidence Retention) requires the Generator Owner to keep data or evidence showing compliance with Requirements R1 through R4, and Measures M1 through M4, for three calendar years.

Application:
    - The clock runs from the creation of the evidence (e.g., the date of the submittal e-mail, the date of the documented-limitation letter, the date of the relay settings record), so retention is a rolling three-year window per record, not a single purge date per audit cycle.
    - The three years is a floor for compliance evidence, not a ceiling. If the Compliance Enforcement Authority requests evidence covering the full period since the last compliance audit and that period is longer than three years, the longer period governs — retain accordingly, or be prepared to reconstruct. Corporate records-retention policy and any state commission retention rule may also require longer; apply the longer of the applicable periods.
    - Records to retain for R1–R4: the written requests received from the PC/TP (M4 requires copies of requests); the dated submittals of applicable protection settings (M4); the relay settings records demonstrating the R1/R2 no-trip-zone settings and any Transmission Planner-permitted alternative; documentation of known regulatory or equipment limitations and the communication of those limitations to the PC and TP, dated (M3); and any PC/TP direction that change reporting is not required.
    - Verification flag: the excerpt set retrieved for the PRC-024-3 PDF did not surface the Compliance/Evidence Retention section itself. The three-calendar-year figure is stated from that section and should be confirmed by reading PRC-024-3's Compliance section (Evidence Retention) before it is quoted in a self-report, audit response, or filing.

=====================================================================
7. THE VSL TRAP — THE SEVERITY BANDS ARE NOT DEADLINES
=====================================================================

The R4 Violation Severity Level grid in the posted standard escalates in bands: more than 60 but less than or equal to 90 calendar days; more than 90 but less than or equal to 120; more than 120 but less than or equal to 150; and failure to provide within 150 calendar days. Those bands grade the severity of a violation that has already occurred. They are not permitted response windows and confer no grace period. A submittal on day 61 is a violation, at the lowest severity band — not compliant performance. Every deadline stated in this deliverable is 60 calendar days, which sits strictly below the first band boundary.

=====================================================================
8. ADJACENT CLOCKS NOT TO BE CONFLATED
=====================================================================

    - R3 (documentation and communication of known regulatory or equipment limitations to the Planning Coordinator and Transmission Planner) runs on its own, shorter clock; the R3 VSL grid in the posted standard begins escalating above 30 calendar days. A limitation documented under R3 does not extend R4's 60 days, and the R4 change-reporting exception does not touch R3.
    - The Quebec interconnection variance in PRC-024-3 addresses Requirement R2 and Attachment 2 (the technical ride-through criteria), not R4's response clock. Check the standard's variance section for any entity-specific variance, but expect no relief from the 60-day submittal requirement.

=====================================================================
9. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY
=====================================================================

    - Version currency: pinned to the PRC-024-3 PDF retrieved 2026-11-23, two days after the as-of date. Confirm no revision became effective on 2026-11-20 or 2026-11-21 before quoting this in a formal filing.
    - Retention figure: confirm the three-calendar-year period against the standard's Compliance section (Evidence Retention) as noted in section 6.
    - Nothing in the retrieved record supports any regional variance, entity-specific agreement, or CEA practice that modifies the 60-calendar-day clocks in R4.

verdict.summary:
# PRC-024-3 — Generator Owner R4 settings delivery, change reporting, and R1–R4 evidence retention

## 0. Source control and scope

- Controlling document: NERC PRC-024-3, *Frequency and Voltage Protection Settings for Generating Resources*, as posted on NERC's reliability-standards page (`nerc.com/globalassets/standards/reliability-standards/prc/prc-024-3.pdf`; retrieved 2026-11-23T20:07:43Z, sha256 `941a2187c37f`). This is the in-force posting, not the 2018-04 project drafts (clean 04172019 / redline to last posted 12052019), which additionally name a "Transmission Owner" in R4/M4. Where they differ, the in-force posting controls: **R4 in force binds the Generator Owner only.**
- Assumption carried from the request: PRC-024-3 is the operative version on 2026-11-21, with no superseding version or errata in force on that date. Verification steps are in §6.
- All three questions are answered from Requirement R4, Measure M4, and the R4 violation-severity table. Requirements R1 and R2 themselves establish the ride-through settings (frequency/voltage no-trip envelope); **R4 is the reporting obligation** and is the provision that carries the time limits.

## 1. Ask 1 — time to provide the R1/R2 settings after a written request

Verbatim R4 (in-force posting):

> "R4. Each Generator Owner shall provide its applicable protection settings associated with Requirements R1 and R2 to the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the associated generating resource(s) within 60 calendar days of receipt of a written request for the data and within 60 calendar days of any change to those previously requested settings unless directed by the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that the reporting of protection setting changes is not required. [Violation Risk Factor: Lower] [Time Horizon: Operations Planning]"

**Answer: 60 calendar days from receipt of the written request.**

Reading points a Generator Owner must apply:

1. **Trigger is receipt, not issuance.** The clock starts when the Generator Owner receives the request. Log the receipt date (email header timestamp, portal receipt, or date stamp on a letter) — that timestamp is the compliance anchor.
2. **Counting.** Treat the receipt date as day 0; the deadline is the receipt date plus 60 calendar days. Worked example: request received 2026-11-21 → deadline 2027-01-20 (9 days remaining in November + 31 in December + 20 in January = 60). If the Generator Owner's procedure counts the receipt date as day 1, the deadline is one day earlier (2027-01-19); use the earlier date.
3. **No business-day carve-out.** PRC-024-3 R4 contains no weekend/holiday extension. Weekends and holidays do not move the deadline; transmit before the weekend/holiday or earlier.
4. **Who may trigger it.** Only the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner *that models the associated generating resource(s)*. A request from any other entity does not start the R4 clock (respond as contractually or otherwise required, but do not book it as an R4 obligation).
5. **What must be provided.** The protection settings associated with R1 and R2 for the modeled resource(s) — the frequency and voltage trip settings and their time delays that define the ride-through characteristic — not the entire relay settings file.

## 2. Ask 2 — deadline and exception after a change to previously requested settings

**Deadline: 60 calendar days from any change to those previously requested settings** — the same 60-calendar-day length as the initial response, restarting from the change, not from the original request.

**Exception (the only one in R4): no reporting is required if the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner directs that the reporting of protection setting changes is not required.**

Application notes:

1. **The direction must come from the requesting PC/TP** — the same entity that made the request. A direction from any other party does not engage the exception.
2. **Get it in writing and keep it.** M4 requires evidence that settings were communicated "such as dated e-mails, correspondence or other evidence and copies of any requests it has received for that information." Store the direction alongside the request it modifies.
3. **Scope of the carve-out.** Textually the "unless directed" clause attaches to the change-reporting obligation; the conservative reading is that it does not excuse the response to the initial written request. If a PC/TP intends to cover both, obtain that in the direction itself.
4. **Withdrawal of a direction.** If the PC/TP later withdraws the direction, the next setting change starts a fresh 60-calendar-day clock; settings changed while the carve-out was in effect should be provided on request.
5. **What counts as a "change."** A change to the settings previously provided — a relay setting change, or a firmware/logic change that alters the R1/R2 characteristic — not merely a change to the planning model.
6. **Enforcement context confirming 60 days is a limit, not a grace period.** The R4 violation-severity table in the in-force posting bands performance as: compliance at 60 calendar days or less; first severity column at more than 60 but less than or equal to 90 calendar days; second column at more than 90 but less than or equal to 120; third column at more than 120 but less than or equal to 150; and the most severe column for failure to provide settings within 150 calendar days of either the written request or the change. The 60-day figure is the requirement boundary; the higher bands are mitigation of penalty, not permission to be late.

## 3. Ask 3 — retention of data or evidence for Requirements R1 through R4 — BLOCKED

**Not answered.** The retention period is not in Requirement R4 or Measure M4; it sits in Section C (Compliance), **Data Retention** subsection, and that section is not among the retrieved passages. The retrieved text covers R3/M3, R4/M4 and the R4 severity table only. Supplying a number would be answering on paper.

How to unblock it (one document read):

1. Open the same in-force posting and go to Section C, Compliance → Data Retention (in PRC-024-2 this was C.1.4).
2. Extract from the paragraph beginning "Each Generator Owner shall keep data or evidence to show compliance with Requirements R1 through R4 …": (a) the period; (b) its unit (years); (c) the comparator phrase, which in the PRC-024 family has been "or since its last compliance audit, whichever is longer"; and (d) whether the 2018-04 project changed either element.
3. For orientation only — **unverified, do not cite**: the PRC-024-2 lineage used three years or since the last compliance audit, whichever is longer. PRC-024-3 must be read on its own text; do not carry the number forward without reading it.
4. Until verified, retain R1–R4 evidence indefinitely (at minimum through the current and next compliance audit cycle) so that no plausible reading of the clause is breached.

## 4. Working procedure — meeting R4 and preserving the evidence

1. **Intake log.** Record for each request: date received, requesting PC/TP, resource IDs, scope of data requested, and whether the requester also directed that change reporting is not required.
2. **Clock.** Day 0 = receipt date. Set the hard deadline at receipt + 60 calendar days; set an internal target of 45 calendar days (comfortably inside the limit); escalate to management at day 30 and again at day 45 if not transmitted.
3. **Assemble.** Pull the R1/R2-associated frequency and voltage protection settings for the modeled resource(s); confirm which units are actually in the model so the response is complete.
4. **Transmit in writing.** Dated email, letter, or portal upload. Retain the transmittal, the settings version transmitted, and the request itself (M4).
5. **Change tracking.** Any change to previously provided settings starts a new 60-calendar-day clock from the change date, unless a written PC/TP direction excuses change reporting; log the direction, its date, and its scope.
6. **Retention.** Apply §3 once verified; pending verification, retain as stated in §3 item 4.

## 5. Answer table

| Ask | Answer | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — time to provide R1/R2 settings after written request | 60 | calendar days from receipt of the written request |
| 2 — deadline and exception after a change | 60 calendar days after any change to previously requested settings; exception: reporting of protection setting changes is not required when the requesting PC/TP so directs | (identifier) |
| 3 — retention for R1–R4 | Blocked — see §3; retention clause not in retrieved evidence | — |

## 6. Verification steps and assumptions that could change the answer

1. **Version in force on 2026-11-21.** Confirm on NERC's reliability-standards page and in the FERC order approving PRC-024-3 (with its stated effective date) that PRC-024-3 — not an earlier or later version — is in force on that date.
2. **Text currency.** Confirm the posting with sha256 `941a2187c37f` is still the current posting on 2026-11-21. If a newer version posts, re-read R4, M4 and the Data Retention subsection before relying on the 60-day figures above.
3. **No regional variance.** PRC-024-3 itself contains no regional variance to the 60-day clock; confirm the Generator Owner's region has not adopted supplemental guidance that tightens it (guidance can shorten, never lengthen, the requirement).
4. **Requester identity.** Confirm the request came from the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the resource; if not, the R4 clock has not started.
5. **Ask 3** remains blocked until the Data Retention subsection is read.

## 1. Authority and version basis
Standard: NERC Reliability Standard PRC-024-3, *Frequency and Voltage Protection Settings for Generating Resources*.
Text relied on: the standard as posted by NERC at https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/standards/reliability-standards/prc/prc-024-3.pdf (retrieved 2026-11-23T20:11:07Z, sha256 prefix 941a2187c37f), i.e., the enforceable text standing on 2026-11-21. The same timeframes appear identically in the 2018-04 project clean draft of 2019-04-17, the 2018-04 redline-to-last-posted of 2019-12-05, and the WECC and AESO postings, so no erratum, interpretation, or regional variant alters any number below. Note the current version's Requirement R4 and its retention bullet are addressed to the *Generator Owner* (the earlier draft's 'Generator Owner or Transmission Owner' phrasing is superseded), which matches the scope of the question. No regional or FCC nuance changes the figures; regional entities (e.g., WECC) enforce the same text.

## 2. Answer to the first value ask — response to a written request (R4)
Requirement R4, sentence 1, provides that each Generator Owner shall provide its applicable protection settings associated with Requirements R1 (generator frequency protective relay settings) and R2 (generator voltage protective relay settings) to the Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the associated generating resource(s) "within 60 calendar days of receipt of a written request for the data".

Answer: **60 calendar days**, counted from **receipt** of the written request (not from the date on the letter), calendar days (not business days). The obligation runs to the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that models the associated generating resource(s). Evidence of compliance is Measure M4: dated e-mails, correspondence or other evidence, plus copies of the requests received.

## 3. Answer to the second value ask — after a change to previously requested settings (R4)
Requirement R4, sentence 1, continues: the Generator Owner shall provide the settings "within 60 calendar days of any change to those previously requested settings **unless directed by the requesting Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner that the reporting of protection setting changes is not required**".

Answer: the post-change deadline is **60 calendar days**, running from the change to the previously requested settings. The single exception is the requester-directed waiver quoted above. Its scope:
- It must come from the *requesting* Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner — the Generator Owner cannot self-exempt.
- It is prospective and per-requester: it waives only the *change-reporting* leg; it does not waive the 60-day response to the original or any future written request.
- It is not self-executing; obtain and retain the direction in writing (dated e-mail/letter) as part of the M4 evidence set so the waiver is auditable.
- It is distinct from the Requirement R3 mechanism. R3 addresses known regulatory or non-protection-system equipment limitations that produce an "exception to Requirements R1 or R2" (i.e., inability to meet the setting criteria), which the Generator Owner must document and communicate to its Planning Coordinator and Transmission Planner within 30 calendar days of identifying the limitation (per Measure M3 and the VSL table). That is a different exception from the R4 change-reporting waiver and neither replaces the other.

## 4. Answer to the third value ask — retention (Requirements R1–R4)
The Compliance section of PRC-024-3 states that the applicable entity shall keep data or evidence to show compliance as identified, unless directed by its Compliance Enforcement Authority to retain specific evidence for a longer period as part of an investigation:
- "The Generator Owner shall keep data or evidence [of] Requirement R1 through R4; for 3 years or until the next audit, whichever is longer."
- "If a Generator Owner is found non-compliant, the Generator Owner ... shall keep information related to the non-compliance until mitigation is complete and approved for the time period specified above, whichever is longer."

Answer: **3 years or until the next audit, whichever is longer**, for data/evidence of Requirements R1 through R4 (not a flat 3 years). Two extensions apply: (a) if a violation is found, retain the non-compliance information until mitigation is complete and approved, and in any case for the period above, whichever is longer; (b) a Compliance Enforcement Authority may direct longer retention of specific evidence during an investigation.

## 5. Requirement / Measure map used
- R1: generator frequency protective relay settings per specified frequency criteria → M1 (dated setting sheets, calibration sheets, or other documentation).
- R2: generator voltage protective relay settings per specified voltage criteria → M2 (dated setting sheets, voltage-time curves, calibration sheets, coordination plots, dynamic simulation studies, etc.).
- R3: document and communicate known regulatory/equipment limitations causing an exception to R1/R2 (within 30 calendar days of identification) → M3 (dated e-mail/letter with study results, event experience, or manufacturer's advice).
- R4: provide applicable R1/R2 settings within 60 calendar days of a written request and within 60 calendar days of any change to previously requested settings, unless the requester directs that change reporting is not required → M4 (dated e-mails/correspondence plus copies of the requests).

## 6. Internal consistency check of every number stated
| Figure | Where stated | Cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| 60 calendar days (request leg) | R4 sentence 1 | Identical to the change-leg figure; the VSL table treats the two legs symmetrically (>60–90, >90–120, >120–150, >150 calendar days = Lower/Severe/Moderate/High VSL bands), confirming 60 is the compliance boundary and that no stated value exceeds or contradicts it. |
| 60 calendar days (change leg) | R4 sentence 1 | Same sentence, same number; the deliverable states no other post-change deadline. |
| Exception (requester direction that change reporting is not required) | R4 sentence 1 | Removes only the change-reporting leg; the 60-day request leg remains, so the answer never understates a deadline. |
| 3 years or until the next audit, whichever is longer | Compliance, retention bullet | The stated rule is the greater of the two operands; the extensions (mitigation-complete-and-approved, CEA direction) only lengthen it, so no retention figure in the deliverable can fall below the standard's floor. |
| 30 calendar days (R3 limitation communication) | R3 / VSL table, cited only as a cross-reference | Clearly separated from the R4 60-day figures; it does not appear in any result value. |

## 7. Operational compliance procedure for a Generator Owner
1. Log every written request from a Planning Coordinator or Transmission Planner on receipt (date-stamp); that date starts the 60-calendar-day clock.
2. Within 60 calendar days of receipt, send the applicable R1 (frequency) and R2 (voltage) settings for the modeled generating resource(s); retain the transmittal and the request copy (M4).
3. On any change to previously requested settings, start a fresh 60-calendar-day clock from the change date and transmit the updated settings, unless the requester has directed in writing that change reporting is not required — in which case file that direction with the request record.
4. Retain all of the above, plus R1–R3 evidence (setting sheets, calibration sheets, limitation documentation/transmittals), for 3 years or until the next audit, whichever is longer; extend to mitigation-complete-and-approved for any non-compliance, and honor any CEA retention direction.

All three reported values (60 calendar days; 60 calendar days with the requester-directed exception; 3 years or until the next audit, whichever is longer) are the values stated above and are drawn verbatim from PRC-024-3 Requirement R4 and its Compliance section as in force on 2026-11-21.
